title: An open door
summary: A deep stack needs a way to pass the signal through unchanged.

cards.text:
A good deep block can choose to do nothing.
The signal walks through an open door.

Swap the usual on-switch for a tip,
and that door often stops being a door.
Extra floors make the stack worse.

question.prompt: What should an open door do to the tips coming in?
question.why: Identity means the output tips match the input tips.
question.simpler: If no setting of the block can do that, you do not have the door.

question.prompt: Fang and colleagues had to change how the shortcut and the block combine.
question.why: The element-wise combination is what made identity easy again.
question.simpler: Depth then helped, past a hundred floors, at few moments.

recall.question: What does an identity path do to the incoming tips?
recall.answer: It can pass them through unchanged.

deeper.note: The paper is Deep Residual Learning in Spiking Neural Networks. The spike-element-wise block is the door.

paper.title: Deep Residual Learning in Spiking Neural Networks
paper.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
paper.section: Why a naive spiking ResNet loses identity, and the SEW block.

terms.plain: a block that can pass spikes through
terms.definition: A residual path whose output can equal its input, so adding depth does not have to make the network worse.
